en.title: GPT-6 Astra Is a Native Visuo-Tactile Policy for Contact-Rich Manipulation
en.deck: Few-shot closed-loop control · 19 contact-rich tasks · UniVTAC & OpenViTac
en.abstract: Can GPT-6 Astra perform contact-rich manipulation and directly use touch as an additional modality? Across 19 simulated tasks in UniVTAC and OpenViTac, Astra achieves mean success rates of 93.8% and 81.8% with a few demonstrations and visual-tactile input. Vision-only performance also exceeds the reported baselines in our comparison. Touch improves several contact decisions, while strong vision reveals alternative cues in tasks previously considered to require tactile information.
en.introTitle: Is contact-rich manipulation still a moat for specialist policies?
intro: Studies including GPT-as-Policy, RoboProbe, RoboDawn and RoboICL[1–7] explore general multimodal models as robot policies: models generate actions from observations, instructions and demonstrations, then revise their decisions through interaction. This offers an alternative to task-specific policy training and raises a fundamental question: what underpins the advantages of specialist models?

Contact-rich manipulation is an important candidate. Precise insertion, stable grasping and material discrimination require more than recognizing objects and their positions: they involve physical information such as contact geometry, slip and material properties. Touch is therefore an important source of sensory information for these tasks. Can general models directly use visual and tactile information to perform contact-rich manipulation, or do these tasks still require specially trained policies?

We investigate this question on UniVTAC[8] and OpenViTac[9]. Using RoboICL[4], we provide GPT-6 Astra with a few demonstrations and compare vision-only and visuo-tactile inputs. We ask two questions: can Astra directly use vision-based tactile images to perform contact-rich manipulation? How well can it perform using vision alone?
en.setupTitle: A general model in the control loop
setup: We evaluate Astra on nineteen simulated tasks from UniVTAC[8] and OpenViTac[9]. Adopted by multiple tactile-policy studies, UniVTAC offers an established evaluation setting with accumulated baselines across eight tasks spanning grasping, placement, classification and precise insertion. The recently introduced OpenViTac includes eleven tasks that further cover physical-property discrimination and precise contact manipulation; its corresponding simulated and real-world tasks, together with the strong correlation between their evaluation results, support the quality of its evaluation framework. We use a 10% stratified sample with sampling seed 42: the sample includes 80 UniVTAC and 130 OpenViTac episodes, including 30 episodes across the three Insert Block v2 shapes.

Our control pipeline builds on RoboICL[4], which organizes demonstrations and online interaction history into observation–action–outcome–observation sequences. This allows a general-purpose model to follow demonstrations and use execution feedback for closed-loop control. We use GPT-6 Astra with xhigh reasoning effort, without training a task-specific policy.

One-shot tasks use 12 segments from a single demonstration. Tasks with distinct material classes or decision branches use two demonstrations with five segments each; Insert Block v2 uses demonstrations of three shapes. Segment length H is selected with reference to task trajectory length and held fixed within each task: 5 by default, 10 for Lift Bottle, Put Bottle, Empty-Can Selection, Grasp Chip, Gear Assembly and Insert Block v1 and v2, and 4 for Grasp Classify. The selected demonstrations remain available throughout the episode.

Within this framework, we compare vision-only (V) and visuo-tactile (V+T) input. V uses visual images alone, while V+T additionally provides left and right tactile RGB images; both conditions use the same demonstrations and evaluation scenes. Camera selection for each task strictly follows the original benchmark’s official configuration. Alongside images, Astra receives robot proprioception and task text, and outputs seven-dimensional actions specifying end-effector translation, rotation and a gripper target.

Some original Grasp Chip success conditions impose unnecessarily strict constraints on execution details. We therefore simplify these conditions: an episode succeeds when the chip remains intact and is grasped, transferred and placed in the target region. All other tasks retain the official success criteria.
result: With visuo-tactile input, Astra achieves mean success rates of 93.8% on UniVTAC and 81.8% on OpenViTac. These exceed the strongest reported baselines in our tables—SimpleTouch at 70.9% and OpenVTLA at 68.7%—by 22.9 and 13.1 percentage points. Vision-only Astra reaches 76.3% and 80.6%, also exceeding the highest baseline mean in each benchmark. Contact-rich manipulation does not establish an irreplaceable capability boundary for specialist models.

The contribution of touch is particularly clear in several tasks. Pull-out Key improves from 30% to 90%, Insert Hole from 60% to 100%, and Hardness Classify from 70% to 90%. These tasks involve contact constraints, precise insertion and material-property judgments, respectively. Their results show that tactile images can supply useful information for Astra’s decisions.
en.visionTitle: Astra’s visual perception can partially substitute for tactile judgments
vision: The two benchmarks show different tactile gains: adding touch improves mean success by 17.5 percentage points on UniVTAC, but by 1.2 points on OpenViTac. This difference may reflect their respective design priorities. UniVTAC emphasizes evaluating the utility of touch and restricts certain visual cues to reduce opportunities for solving tasks through vision alone; most tasks, for example, omit the wrist camera. OpenViTac places greater emphasis on alignment with real-world manipulation, providing both fixed and wrist cameras across all tasks and preserving richer visual information. For Astra, these cues may support some judgments otherwise associated with touch, reducing the additional benefit of tactile input.

Grasp Classify, Roughness Classify and Roughness-Guided Regrasp illustrate this effect: vision-only success is 100% on all three. Audited Grasp Classify frames show visible surface texture on the rough cylinder. In Roughness Classify, the wrist camera reveals ridges and a jagged silhouette on rough objects. In Roughness-Guided Regrasp, surface ridges are discernible even from the fixed camera, allowing Astra to select the rough object before contact. The policy’s action notes also refer to these visual differences.

Astra uses fine-grained visual cues to solve some tasks considered touch-dependent, demonstrating a capacity for vision-only substitution not evident in previously reported specialist-model results. A “tactile task” therefore does not necessarily require touch. As several tasks approach perfect scores, future benchmarks should control visual cues that can substitute for touch and introduce visually unobservable physical properties, tighter manipulation tolerances, and more complex contact and recovery sequences to distinguish models’ tactile understanding and manipulation capabilities.

Analysis of tasks whose success rates decreased with tactile input reveals misinterpretation of weak load cues and repeated probing that consumed the action budget, alongside possible stochastic variation. In the three paired Weight Classify cases where vision alone succeeded and visuo-tactile input failed, Astra interpreted small tactile shear or contact patterns resembling the light-object reference as evidence of a light load, misclassifying heavy objects. The vision-only runs instead reached the correct judgment from visible slip after relaxing the grasp. In Empty-Can Selection, subtle tactile changes likewise led to incorrect weight judgments, while repeated comparisons consumed the action budget and left some transfers incomplete. These cases identify the interpretation of weak tactile cues and the efficiency of probing as important factors in performance.

takeawayPoints.title: Contact-rich manipulation is not a moat for specialist models.
takeawayPoints.body: Astra achieves mean success rates of 93.8% on UniVTAC and 81.8% on OpenViTac, substantially outperforming the reported specialist baselines in our comparison.

takeawayPoints.title: Touch is not exclusive to specialist models.
takeawayPoints.body: Without task-specific training, Astra directly interprets and uses tactile images, achieving better overall performance than the reported specialist VTLA baselines in our comparison.

takeawayPoints.title: Vision can replace some tactile judgments.
takeawayPoints.body: Vision-only Astra achieves 100% on three texture-related tasks, revealing visual cues previously overlooked by specialist models.

takeawayPoints.title: Vision-based tactile sensing is a promising direction.
takeawayPoints.body: Image representations of contact connect directly to general visual capabilities and may scale alongside foundation models.

takeawayPoints.title: Parts of current benchmarks are approaching saturation.
takeawayPoints.body: More challenging contact-rich evaluations should control visual shortcuts and better distinguish the capabilities of general-purpose models.

en.conclusionSummary: Contact-rich manipulation and tactile perception are not inherent moats for specialist policies. With only a few demonstrations, GPT-6 Astra directly uses vision-based tactile images to outperform the reported specialist baselines in our comparison across two benchmarks, while exhibiting active probing, fine adjustment and manipulation recovery. Its vision-only performance also reveals cues that can substitute for touch in existing evaluations. Yet interpreting tangential motion and forces, estimating spatial relationships and correcting motion under contact constraints remain inconsistent. Future work should incorporate vision-based tactile sensing into joint pretraining with visual inputs and explore how these capabilities scale alongside foundation models. Tasks involving physical properties that cannot be distinguished visually, tighter manipulation tolerances and real-robot experiments will help establish whether these capabilities translate into reliable physical interaction.
en.mainResultTitle: Astra outperforms specialist policies by a wide margin on contact-rich tasks
en.tactileTitle: Astra demonstrates strong capabilities in interpreting and using tactile information
mainResults: With visuo-tactile input, Astra achieves mean success rates of 93.8% on UniVTAC and 81.8% on OpenViTac. These exceed the strongest reported baselines in our tables—SimpleTouch at 70.9% and OpenVTLA at 68.7%—by 22.9 and 13.1 percentage points. Vision-only Astra reaches 76.3% and 80.6%, also exceeding the highest baseline mean in each benchmark. Contact-rich manipulation therefore does not constitute an exclusive domain of capability for specialist models.
tactileResults: As shown in Figure 2, adding touch improves success rates on six tasks. On UniVTAC, Pull-out Key rises from 30% to 90%, Lift Can from 80% to 100%, Insert Hole from 60% to 100%, and Insert HDMI from 50% to 80%. On OpenViTac, Hardness Classify improves from 70% to 90%, and Insert Block v1 from 40% to 70%. Spanning contact constraints, grasping, precise insertion and material-property judgments, these gains show that Astra can effectively use tactile information in few-shot control without additional tactile-policy training. However, vision-only and visuo-tactile inputs yield equal success rates on several tasks, including Grasp Classify, Roughness Classify and Roughness-Guided Regrasp. Adding touch even reduces success rates on Weight Classify, Empty-Can Selection, Insert Tube and Insert Block v2. Section 3.3 examines possible explanations for these observations.

The videos below compare vision-only and visuo-tactile performance on the six tasks whose success rates improve with touch. Action notes related to touch are highlighted in red to illustrate how Astra uses tactile information to guide manipulation.

en.costSummary: The visuo-tactile evaluation used approximately 59% more tokens and incurred 42% higher costs than the vision-only evaluation. Cached tokens accounted for over 80% of input tokens in both groups, allowing most inputs to be reused through caching. Together, the two evaluations consumed approximately 336 million tokens at a cost of CNY 7,505.

Median latency is 15.4 seconds for vision-only input and 14.0 seconds for visuo-tactile input; 90% of valid requests complete within 46.3 and 44.0 seconds, respectively. Latency is the complete API response time recorded in provider logs, including server and gateway waiting time but excluding simulation execution.

en.showcaseIntro: Beyond aggregate success rates, Astra exhibits striking behaviors during execution. The following eight visuo-tactile examples illustrate tactile inference, active probing, fine adjustment and manipulation recovery. Red text highlights tactile cues in the action notes.
limitations: The preceding examples demonstrate Astra’s perceptual and manipulation capabilities, but these capabilities remain inconsistent under complex contact conditions. Four limitations emerge: limited sensitivity to tangential motion and forces can lead to misinterpretation of subtle tactile cues; fine spatial relationships can be estimated inaccurately; plausible corrective intentions may not translate into effective actions; and repeated probing does not necessarily produce reliable convergence.

The following three visuo-tactile failures illustrate difficulties in physical-property inference, fine alignment and correction, and active probing. Together with the successful examples, they show that the challenge extends beyond proposing a plausible strategy to estimating contact state accurately and translating that judgment into reliable actions.

zh.title: GPT-6 Astra：适用于接触密集型操作的原生视觉—触觉策略
zh.deck: Few-shot 闭环控制 · 19 项接触密集型操作任务 · UniVTAC 与 OpenViTac
zh.abstract: GPT-6 Astra 能否直接胜任接触密集型操作，并利用触觉这一额外模态？在 UniVTAC 与 OpenViTac 的 19 项仿真任务中，Astra 仅凭少量示范，在视觉与触觉输入下达到 93.8% 和 81.8% 的平均成功率。纯视觉表现同样超过所比较的已报告基线；触觉进一步改善多项接触决策，而强大的视觉能力也揭示了部分任务中可替代触觉的线索。
zh.introTitle: 接触密集型操作，是否仍是专用策略的护城河？
intro: GPT-as-Policy、RoboProbe、RoboDawn 和 RoboICL 等工作[1–7]探索了通用多模态模型作为机器人策略的能力：模型直接根据观测、指令与示范生成动作，并在交互过程中持续修正决策。这类方法为机器人操作提供了不同于任务专用策略训练的路径，也促使我们重新审视专用模型的优势究竟来自哪里。
接触密集型操作是一个重要候选。精细插入、稳定夹持与材料辨别不仅要求理解物体的外观和位置，还涉及接触几何、滑移及材料属性等物理信息，触觉因而成为支持这类操作的重要感知手段。因此，一个自然的问题是：通用模型能否直接利用视觉与触觉信息完成接触密集型操作，还是说，这类任务仍需要专门训练的策略？
本文在 UniVTAC[8] 与 OpenViTac[9] 上研究这一问题。我们采用 RoboICL[4] 框架，将少量示范直接提供给 GPT-6 Astra，并比较纯视觉与视觉—触觉两种输入条件。实验关注两个问题：Astra 能否直接利用视触觉图像完成接触密集型操作？仅凭视觉输入，其操作能力又能达到什么水平？
zh.setupTitle: 把通用模型放进控制闭环
setup: 我们在 UniVTAC[8] 与 OpenViTac[9] 的十九项仿真任务上评测 Astra。UniVTAC 已被多项触觉策略研究采用，涵盖八项抓取、放置、分类与精细插入任务，具有较成熟的评测与基线积累。新近提出的 OpenViTac 包含十一项任务，进一步覆盖物理属性辨别与精细接触操作；其仿真与真机任务的对应设计，以及二者评测结果之间较强的相关性，为评测质量提供了支撑。评测采用随机种子 42 的 10% 分层抽样，包含 UniVTAC 的 80 集与 OpenViTac 的 130 集，其中 Insert Block v2 的三种形状共 30 集。
控制流程基于 RoboICL[4]：该框架将示范与在线交互历史组织为“观测—动作—执行结果—后续观测”，使通用模型能够参考示范，并根据执行反馈进行闭环控制。我们以 GPT-6 Astra 为策略模型，推理强度设置为 xhigh，不训练任务专用策略。

单示范（one-shot）任务从一条示范中选取 12 个片段；存在不同材料类别或决策分支的任务提供两条示范，每条选取 5 个片段；Insert Block v2 提供三种形状的示范。片段长度 H 参考任务轨迹长度设置，并在同一任务内保持固定：默认 5；Lift Bottle、Put Bottle、Empty-Can Selection、Grasp Chip、Gear Assembly 与Insert Block v1 和 v2为 10；Grasp Classify 为 4。选定示范在整集操作中持续可见。
在此框架下，我们比较纯视觉（V）与视觉—触觉（V+T）两种输入条件：V 仅使用视觉图像，V+T 额外提供左右触觉 RGB 图像，两组采用相同的示范与评测场景。各任务的相机选择严格遵循原 benchmark 的官方配置。除图像外，Astra 还接收机器人自身状态与任务文本，输出包含末端平移、旋转与夹爪目标的七维动作。
Grasp Chip 的部分原始判定条件对操作细节施加了不必要的严格约束。因此，我们简化了这些条件：只要薯片能够保持完整，完成抓取、转移并放置到目标区域，即判为成功。其余任务均沿用官方成功判定。
zh.resultTitle: 整体表现与视觉—触觉能力
result: 在视觉—触觉输入下，Astra 在 UniVTAC 与 OpenViTac 上的平均成功率分别为 93.8% 和 81.8%，较表中最强的已报告基线 SimpleTouch（70.9%）与 OpenVTLA（68.7%）分别高出 22.9 和 13.1 个百分点。纯视觉 Astra 也达到 76.3% 和 80.6%，超过两组基线的最高平均值。接触密集型操作并未构成专用模型不可替代的能力边界。
触觉的价值在部分任务中较为明确：Pull-out Key 的成功率由 30% 提升至 90%，Insert Hole 由 60% 提升至 100%，Hardness Classify 由 70% 提升至 90%。这些任务分别涉及接触约束、精细插入与材料属性判断，结果表明触觉图像能够为 Astra 提供有效的决策信息。
zh.visionTitle: Astra 的视觉感知能力可部分替代触觉判断
vision: 两个 benchmark 呈现出不同的触觉收益：UniVTAC 中，加入触觉使平均成功率提高 17.5 个百分点；OpenViTac 中则提高 1.2 个百分点。这一差异可能与二者的设计侧重点有关。UniVTAC 注重验证触觉信息的有效性，通过限制部分视觉线索，减少仅凭视觉完成任务的可能，例如多数任务不提供腕相机。OpenViTac 则更强调与真实操作场景的对齐，所有任务均提供固定相机与腕相机，保留了较为充分的视觉信息。对于具备强大视觉感知能力的 Astra，这些线索可能支持部分原本依赖触觉的判断，从而减小触觉带来的额外收益。

Grasp Classify、Roughness Classify 与 Roughness-Guided Regrasp 提供了直观例证：三项任务的纯视觉成功率均为 100%。在已审查的图像中，Grasp Classify 的粗糙圆柱具有可见表面纹理；Roughness Classify 的腕相机能呈现粗糙物体的棱纹与锯齿状轮廓；Roughness-Guided Regrasp 中，物体表面的棱纹在固定相机下也可辨识，Astra 在接触前便据此选择粗糙物体。策略输出的动作说明也提到了这些视觉差异。
Astra 能够利用细粒度视觉线索完成部分原本被视为依赖触觉的任务，展现出此前专用模型的已报告结果尚未体现的纯视觉替代能力。这也说明，“触觉任务”并不必然需要触觉。随着多项任务接近满分，未来的 benchmark 应控制可替代触觉的视觉线索，并引入视觉不可辨识的物理属性、更严格的操作公差及更复杂的接触与恢复过程，以区分模型的触觉理解与操作能力。

对加入触觉后成功率下降的任务进行分析发现，除可能的随机波动外，还存在对微弱载荷线索的误读和反复探测消耗操作预算的问题。在 Weight Classify 的三组纯视觉成功、视觉—触觉失败的配对案例中，Astra 将触觉图像中较小的剪切形变或类似轻物体的接触图案解释为轻载，误判了重物体；纯视觉版本则通过松夹后的可见滑移作出正确判断。Empty-Can Selection 中，细微触觉变化同样导致了错误的重量判断，反复比较两罐也消耗了操作预算，使部分案例未能完成转移。这些案例反映出，弱触觉线索的辨识与探测效率仍是影响表现的重要因素。

zh.conclusionSummary: 接触密集型操作与触觉感知并非专用策略的固有护城河。GPT-6 Astra 仅凭少量示范，即可直接利用视触觉图像，在两个 benchmark 上超过所比较的已报告专用模型基线，并展现出主动探测、精细调整和操作恢复能力；其纯视觉表现也揭示了现有评测中可替代触觉的线索。与此同时，切向运动与受力的辨识、空间估计和接触修正仍不稳定。未来应将视触觉与视觉一同纳入通用模型的联合预训练，探索其随基础模型共同扩展的潜力，并通过涉及视觉不可辨识物理属性的任务、更严格的操作公差及真实机器人实验，检验这些能力能否转化为可靠的物理交互。
zh.mainResultTitle: Astra 在接触密集型任务中断崖式领先
zh.tactileTitle: Astra 具备强大的触觉理解与利用能力
mainResults: 在视觉—触觉输入下，Astra 在 UniVTAC 与 OpenViTac 上的平均成功率分别为 93.8% 和 81.8%，较表中最强的已报告基线 SimpleTouch（70.9%）与 OpenVTLA（68.7%）分别高出 22.9 和 13.1 个百分点。纯视觉 Astra 也达到 76.3% 和 80.6%，超过两组基线的最高平均值。接触密集型操作并未构成专用模型不可替代的能力边界。
tactileResults: 如图 2 所示，加入触觉后，六项任务的成功率得到提升：UniVTAC 中，Pull-out Key 由 30% 提升至 90%，Lift Can 由 80% 提升至 100%，Insert Hole 由 60% 提升至 100%，Insert HDMI 由 50% 提升至 80%；OpenViTac 中，Hardness Classify 由 70% 提升至 90%，Insert Block v1 由 40% 提升至 70%。这些任务涵盖接触约束、抓取、精细插入与材料属性判断，表明 Astra 无需额外训练触觉策略，即可在少样本控制中有效利用触觉信息。不过，在 Grasp Classify、Roughness Classify、Roughness-Guided Regrasp 等多个任务中，纯视觉与视觉—触觉输入的表现持平；在 Weight Classify、Empty-Can Selection、Insert Tube 和 Insert Block v2 中，加入触觉后的成功率甚至有所下降。我们将在 3.3 节进一步分析这些现象的可能原因。
下方展示加入触觉后成功率提升的六项任务的视频对比。其中，与触觉相关的动作说明以红色标出，以展示 Astra 如何利用触觉信息辅助操作。
zh.visionVideoIntro: 下方展示三项纯视觉与视觉—触觉成功率均为 100% 的分类与选择任务。动作说明中的关键视觉线索以绿色标出，关键触觉线索以红色标出，以对比 Astra 在两种输入下作出判断的依据。
zh.declineVideoIntro: 下方展示 Weight Classify 与 Empty-Can Selection 中纯视觉成功、视觉—触觉失败的配对案例。绿色标出可见滑移等关键视觉线索，红色标出模型用于重量判断的触觉线索。
zh.costSummary: 视觉—触觉组的总 token 用量比纯视觉组高约 59%，费用高约 42%。两组输入 token 的缓存命中比例均超过 80%，大部分输入可通过缓存复用。两组评测合计消耗约 3.36 亿 token，费用约 7,505 元。
zh.latencySummary: 两组单次响应延时分布接近，均呈现长尾。纯视觉与视觉—触觉组的中位数分别为 15.4 秒和 14.0 秒，90% 的有效请求分别在 46.3 秒和 44.0 秒内完成。这里统计日志记录的完整 API 响应耗时，包含服务端与网关等待，不含仿真执行时间。
zh.latencyCaption: 图 3 · 单次 API 响应延时分布。仅统计成功且有输出 token 的请求，按 5 秒分箱，概率以各组全部有效请求为分母；超过 120 秒的比例分别为 0.76%（V）与 0.47%（V+T）。
zh.showcaseIntro: 除整体成功率外，Astra 在执行过程中还展现出一些令人印象深刻的细节。下方展示触觉推断、主动探测、精细调整和操作恢复四类行为的八个视觉—触觉案例，红色标出动作说明中的触觉线索。
limitations: 上述案例展示了 Astra 的感知与操作能力，但这些能力在复杂接触条件下仍不稳定。当前局限主要体现在四个方面：对切向运动和受力变化不够敏感，可能误读微弱触觉线索；精细空间关系的估计仍有偏差；合理的调整意图未必转化为有效动作；反复试探也未必带来稳定收敛。
下方展示三个视觉—触觉失败案例，分别说明物理属性推断、精细对准与修正，以及主动探测策略中的问题。它们与前述成功案例共同表明，关键挑战不仅是提出合理的操作思路，还包括准确估计接触状态，并将判断转化为可靠的动作。

goal.zh: 夹住横放的罐体，将其抬起并调整为直立姿态。
goal.en: Grasp the horizontal can, lift it and reorient it upright.

Test retention with a slow 5 mm lift, keeping the can pinched and watching for relative motion.
Continue a gentle lift with a small motion toward the can, allowing its far end to remain supported as it begins to tip.

Continue the controlled tipping lift, maintaining the pinch while the can's far end remains near the support.

Maintain the grasp and continue the smooth rising arc toward the far end; the can is still oblique rather than upright.
Keep the can pinched while lifting more slowly and progressing toward its base to increase the upright angle.

Continue the slow tipping arc with the current pinch. The can's lower end remains close to the support, so release is premature.
Shift the held end over the can's base with a smaller upward component; retain the pinch until the body is nearly vertical.

Close gradually around the horizontal can while holding the initial hand pose; check bilateral contact before lifting.

notes.text: Approach a snug grasp with smaller closure increments, monitoring both tactile views for contact.
tactileHighlights: monitoring both tactile views for contact.

notes.text: Raise slightly while continuing the smooth world-Y turn, keeping the can clear of the support surface and the grasp unchanged.

Continue the slow turn at constant height; the can is securely following the fingers and its axis is approaching vertical.

goal.zh: 调整杆的姿态并将其插入目标孔中。
goal.en: Align the rod and insert it into the target hole.

Approach the candidate 30-degree-from-vertical slant using the entrance as a pivot; preserve the existing grip.

Continue a small vertical approach; tactile bands are still almost level, so the slant is not yet clear.

notes.text: Lower in millimeter steps with the grasp unchanged, monitoring for asymmetric contact rather than assuming a hole direction.
Continue gentle descent; the tube remains at the entrance and contact tilt is still small.
Approach a little farther vertically, keeping the grip and orientation steady while looking for directional tactile shear.

notes.text: Slow the vertical approach as contact develops; retain the tube without changing wrist orientation.

tactileHighlights: consistent mirrored contact.

notes.text: Advance along the inferred slant. The exposed tube is shortening while its tactile angle stays stable, consistent with entry into the bore.
tactileHighlights: its tactile angle stays stable, consistent with entry into the bore.

notes.text: Continue steady insertion in positive X and downward, maintaining the stable contact angle and watching exposed tube length.

goal.zh: 调整 HDMI 插头的姿态与位置，将其插入插座。
goal.en: Align the HDMI plug with the socket and insert it.

Square the plug axis while compensating tip motion and approach the visible socket opening; retain the existing grip.

Continue a shallow straight insertion with the plug visually centered, retaining the grip and monitoring its contact with the slot.

Approach the visible opening at the revised depth position in a two-millimeter descent, holding orientation and grip fixed to compare tip motion with hand motion.

The connector body has stopped following hand descent. Slightly reduce the opening target and lift clear to check retention before correcting angular alignment.
The lifted connector follows the hand and is centered laterally. Approach the opening again with the slightly smaller grip target, leaving angular and depth-axis alignment unchanged to check entry.
Close the small visible gap with a controlled 1.5 mm descent at the current alignment and tighter grasp, then inspect whether the connector follows into the opening.
Lift clear of possible rim contact and make a small pitch correction, compensating hand translation to keep the plug tip near the opening's depth position.
The lifted plug is retained with a visible gap above the slot. Approach at the corrected pitch with a short vertical descent, preserving lateral centering.
Try a shallow seating increment at the corrected pitch. Watch the upper connector body as the tip becomes occluded, maintaining the tighter grip.
The visible tip again stops above the opening. Lift clear and test a small depth correction toward the camera, opposite the earlier unsuccessful depth adjustments, while retaining the current pitch.
Approach at the revised depth and pitch, adding a submillimeter leftward correction to center the visible tip over the slot. Keep the connector grasped.
Lift slightly and shift two millimeters toward the camera to test the remaining depth-axis alignment; lateral centering looks close, but entry is not confirmed.
Lower through the visible gap at the latest depth correction, keeping pitch and lateral centering fixed. Check whether the connector enters or stops on the rim.
Try a shallow seating increment at the latest depth alignment. Keep the retained plug centered and monitor for entry; the tip is hidden by the socket.
Entry remains unconfirmed after depth adjustments. Withdraw and test the opposite pitch correction, compensating translation approximately to preserve tip alignment while clear of the rim.
Approach the visible slot with the revised pitch and a one-millimeter depth correction, keeping the retained plug laterally centered.

latency.source: Provider RT(ms), from deduplicated and reconciled evaluation-phase logs.

notes.text: Torsional deformation has relaxed. Hold the attained angle and begin a slow, straight upward extraction without lateral motion.

tactileHighlights: The tactile patches shifted during the lift, suggesting axial resistance.

notes.text: Test a small straight pull at the relaxed angle; compare tactile patch motion to distinguish release from continued axial loading.
tactileHighlights: compare tactile patch motion to distinguish release from continued axial loading.

tactileHighlights: Pause at the small extraction offset to distinguish transient tactile lag from sustained axial resistance, keeping orientation and grasp unchanged.

caption.zh: 从细微形变到阻力判断。Astra 根据触觉扭转变形识别机械止挡，回转卸载后试拔；遇到阻力时重新落座并细调角度，还主动停顿以观察形变是否消退。值得关注的是，它利用接触反馈决定何时继续、何时卸载与等待，而非持续增加拉力。
caption.en: From subtle deformation to resistance-aware control. Astra identifies a mechanical stop from tactile torsion, unwinds, and tests extraction. When resistance persists, it reseats the key, refines the angle, and pauses to observe whether deformation subsides. The notable behavior is using contact feedback to decide when to advance, unload, or wait, rather than simply increasing the pull.

caption.zh: 从接触变化推断孔道方向。轻触孔口后，Astra 将两侧触觉条纹的相反倾斜与杆的可见偏转结合，判断孔道方向与参考示范相反，再调整倾角并沿孔轴插入。该案例的亮点是从局部接触线索推断隐含几何，并据此改变示范中的运动方向。
caption.en: Inferring bore direction from contact. After probing the entrance, Astra combines opposite slopes in the two tactile bands with visible shaft deflection to infer a bore direction mirrored relative to the reference. It then pivots the shaft and inserts along that axis. The notable behavior is using local contact cues to infer hidden geometry and adapt the demonstrated motion direction.

goal.zh: 辨别物体的软硬属性，并转移到对应的目标区域。
goal.en: Determine the object’s hardness and move it to the corresponding target region.

caption.en: Actively probing material properties. After securing its grasp, Astra slightly relaxes its grasp to compare tactile responses. It resecures the object after detecting slip, then judges hardness from the loaded contact edge. The notable behavior is actively seeking discriminative information while restoring grasp stability in response to the object’s motion.

caption.zh: 在初次接触附近逐步收敛夹持。Astra 发现单侧先接触后，先做半毫米横向修正，再以更小幅度闭合；待两侧均出现接触后，停止继续夹紧并轻抬验证。其亮点是把易碎物体抓取拆解为对中、轻触、双侧支撑和试提几个细致步骤，避免将持续夹紧当作抓稳的唯一方式。
caption.en: Converging cautiously on a fragile grasp. After one fingertip makes contact first, Astra applies a half-millimeter lateral correction and narrows the jaws in smaller increments. Once bilateral contact appears, it stops tightening and tests retention with a gentle lift. The notable behavior is separating centering, light contact, bilateral support, and test lifting instead of relying on continued closure to secure the object.

goal.en: Seat the red gear on the spindle and rotate it in engagement with its paired gear.

caption.en: Separating spindle alignment from tooth engagement. When the gear tilts, Astra unloads and corrects its center. After further obstruction, it adjusts yaw to address possible tooth-on-tooth interference, then seats and rotates the gear. The notable behavior is addressing distinct assembly constraints through successive corrections informed by the object’s response to contact.

caption.en: Distinguishing hand motion from insertion. Astra observes that the metal connector remains exposed while tactile contact shifts, identifying finger slip along a blocked plug. It unloads, recenters, and applies a submillimeter correction. This illustrates careful verification of physical progress: reaching a hand target does not establish that the object has been inserted.

The notable behavior is combining grasp-pose preparation with local contact-responsive correction, resolving obstruction through a small retreat and realignment.

goal.zh: 通过交互判断物体的轻重，并转移至对应托盘。
goal.en: Determine whether the object is light or heavy through interaction and transfer it to the corresponding tray.

caption.zh: 触觉变化小，并不必然意味着物体轻。该重物体在抬升后表现出较小的触觉剪切，Astra 据此将其判断为轻物体，并放到了错误的蓝色托盘。接触图案还会受到夹持位置、开合程度和运动状态影响；模型虽然能够描述图像变化，但从弱线索推断物理属性仍可能出错。
caption.en: Small tactile changes do not necessarily imply a light object. After lifting this heavy block, Astra interprets the limited tactile shear as evidence of low weight and places it on the incorrect blue tray. Contact patterns also depend on grasp location, aperture, and motion. Describing an image change therefore does not guarantee a reliable inference about the underlying physical property.

caption.zh: 识别出姿态错误，仍未能稳定完成修正。立方体多次搁在孔沿，Astra 重新抓取并尝试调平；第 240 步起输出的一组俯仰修正指令累计约 51.6°，同时补偿平移，最终仍因达到步数上限而失败。该过程体现了识别对准问题与可靠执行修正之间的差距：修正幅度、旋转中心和接触约束需要协调处理。这里的角度为指令累计值，而非物体实际转角。
caption.en: Recognizing misorientation does not ensure a successful correction. The cube repeatedly rests on the rim, prompting regrasping and leveling attempts. The pitch commands beginning at step 240 sum to approximately 51.6°, with accompanying translation compensation, yet the episode reaches its action limit without successful insertion. The sequence illustrates the gap between identifying misalignment and reliably correcting it: adjustment magnitude, rotation center, and contact constraints must be coordinated. The angle is a commanded sum, not a measured object rotation.

caption.zh: 最终判断正确，但未能及时完成操作。Astra 先比较松夹时的释放阈值，再转向支撑与抬升状态下的触觉变化；发现接触不稳定后，又更换抓取高度重复比较。直到第 370 步才选中正确的蓝罐，第 390 步开始抓取并抬升，随后耗尽 400 步预算，未完成转移。这反映出主动探测虽能提供信息，但探测次数、停止条件与剩余操作之间的协调仍不充分。
caption.en: A correct eventual choice comes too late to complete the task. Astra first compares release thresholds, then tactile changes between supported and lifted states. Unstable contact leads to another comparison at a different grasp height. It selects the correct blue can at step 370 and begins grasping and lifting at step 390, but exhausts the 400-action budget before transfer. Active probing can yield useful information, yet the number of probes, stopping criterion, and remaining manipulation steps are not always well coordinated.
